verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I've been feeling really anxious over the past few months" and later clarifies it started "maybe about two months or so" and has "felt it get worse and worse over the past".
Patient: "I just get really nervous every morning about leaving the house" indicating daily morning anxiety and fear about leaving the house.

Patient: "maybe about two months or so... that's probably coincides with me starting a new job, which I would say it's quite stressful" and "My boss is not very nice to me." Job is in fashion retail head office team.
Patient: "I can't get to sleep for hours and hours and hours" and "maybe three, four hours I'm getting now" and describes it as "such a shallow sleep."
Patient: "in the daytime... it's just really, really low" when asked about energy levels.
Patient: "I find no enjoyment at all kind of day to day in anything that I'm doing" which is consistent with anhedonia.

Palpitations: "usually... in the morning"; feels "just a constant, like, rapid heart beating"; describes rhythm as "Irregular, I think"; duration "a couple of minutes" to "like, 10 minutes"; chest discomfort: "Well, yeah, it's painful when... my heart is being fat [fast]."

For palpitations: "this is only in the past sort of like, couple of months as I say that I've been experiencing this." For anxiety: "Before this, did you have Any similar times... ?" Patient: "Not really, no... I've never felt anything that's bad before."

Patient: "I'm pretty much down. Like, I don't enjoy being with my day at all because I'm just so worried about everything" and links it to work stress throughout; she says work is "really stressful" and anxiety is mainly work-focused.
Patient: "I find no enjoyment at all kind of day to day in anything that I'm doing" and later: "anything that previously was really fun is just not enjoyable."
Patient: "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts or any thoughts that have been that extreme."

Friends: "I avoid them in so much that... I know that I'm not going to have fun because I don't want to go out"; Hobbies: "I did used to like to go running and to play tennis... but now... I'm not going out to do that quite so much."

Work: "Has it ever got so bad that you've actually had to miss work?" Patient: "No"; also "I think that would just add to the tension" and "I wonder if it's building up... I'm worried it's building up to that." She also dreads work: "I just really dread going there."
Patient: "Probably not. Significant changes, maybe? No, I wouldn't say that... I'm eating, like, much differently. Oh. I probably have more chocolate than normal just because I feel so down."

Patient does not report avoiding all public places but says: "I find public transport really stressful in a way, especially being on the tube because it's quite getting warmer, so it's just really airless."

Therapy: "I've never done that before" (re: one to one therapy) and agrees she would be happy to have it. She has discussed with her mother: "I talked to my mum because she also suffers from... depression... she recommended that I come to the gp."
When asked who she lives with: Patient: "Yeah, I live with my parents. With my parents."

Alcohol: "probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday... I probably go over my limit just on those days anyway. And then like maybe a glass of wine during the week." This implies above recommended limits on weekends plus midweek wine.
Smoking: "I try not to smoke, but I do occasionally" which matches occasional smoker.
Illicit drugs: To "Do you smoke or take any other drugs or anything?" Patient: "I try not to smoke, but I do occasionally, but I don't take them." (denies taking other drugs).
Patient: "I have a good support system. Like, I do have a good family and stuff" indicating good family support.
Patient: "I talked to my mum because she also suffers from, or she's suffered from like depression in the past."
The transcript contains no physical examination or vital signs; it is entirely history and plan, so stating none are documented is accurate.

Work-related anxiety: symptoms started with stressful new job; morning anticipatory anxiety about leaving the house and being late; palpitations described; functional impairment (sleep, social life, hobbies) but "I've always managed to make it to work" (no avoidance); denies suicidal thoughts. The doctor frames it as anxiety and discusses anxiety management.

Insomnia secondary to anxiety: patient reports difficulty initiating sleep for "hours and hours," only "three, four hours" of shallow sleep, clearly in context of anxiety about work; doctor links anxiety and offers sleep advice.

Doctor: "In terms of palpitations, it is most likely to be associated with anxiety"; asks about chest pain and patient replies essentially pain only when heart is beating fast; patient describes irregular sensation. Fact’s mention of rare chest discomfort matches "it's painful when... my heart is being fast."
Doctor: "start you can self refer via the NHS for what we call like talking therapy, which is a type of behavioral therapy"—this corresponds to CBT-type talking therapy referral via NHS.
Doctor: "there are some online resources that are really helpful. Put the details on there and you can get on with them straight away."
Doctor: "I'll put some more information on your notes about helping with your sleep patterns and things like that" indicating discussion/information on sleep hygiene.
Doctor: "it's probably worth having a couple of basic blood tests just to make sure that there's not something triggering that off" (re: palpitations).
Doctor: "then arranging a GP follow up a week after you've had the test so we can just go through the results with you."

Doctor: "if you're feeling like it's not helping at all or your anxiety is getting worse to the point where you can't cope with work or you can't just do your normal things day to day, then it's important for you to give us a call back and just discuss that further."
As above, doctor plans: "arranging a GP follow up a week after you've had the test so we can just go through the results with you."
As above, doctor advises return "if... your anxiety is getting worse to the point where you can't cope with work or you can't just do your normal things day to day."
